overall_summary: Deduplication of 47 unique Shorts reveals an overwhelming viewer preference for high-stakes, first-person exoplanetary survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic anomalies, consistently generating 800-1,050+ views and 3.5%+ like ratios at 19-21s durations. Conversely, standard psychology trivia ('Brain Can Create Fake Memories', earworms) and recycled animal facts repeatedly flatlined under 100 views. Reposting identical or near-identical scripts multiple times severely suppressed algorithmic distribution.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Cosmic Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,028 views, 36 likes) represent the channel's highest traction tier.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor production in immersive 19-21s survival scenarios exploring hostile, bizarre celestial bodies with visceral second-person pacing.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (723 views, 25 likes) outperform static declarative facts.
winning_patterns.action: Lead with counter-intuitive physical phenomena framed through extreme tangible consequences rather than dry encyclopedic definitions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple re-uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' achieved 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' stalled at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Cease low-stakes cognitive trivia micro-facts unless embedded within a high-stakes psychological mystery or survival narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted 3 times dropped from 220 to 87 to 34 views; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' repeated with diminishing impact.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce a strict anti-repetition registry; every Short must tackle an unreleased subject with fresh narrative architecture.

next_video.hook_style: Visceral first-person survival threat with a physical impossibility hook
next_video.concept: What If You Got Within 1,000 Kilometers of a Magnetar?
next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-action at 0:00: 'If you drifted within 1,000 kilometers of a magnetar, you wouldn't be crushed by gravity—your chemistry would simply dissolve.'
next_video.twist_direction: At 0:13, reveal that the magnetic field is so intensely powerful that it stretches every atom in your body into needle-thin cylinders, instantly wiping your bio-electrical nerve signals before pain can even register.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-retention 'What If' cosmic danger mechanic that drives the channel's 1,000+ view tier, while pivoting to a completely untouched, scientifically staggering entity (magnetars/SGR 1806-20).
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond planets (55 Cancri e), burning ice (Gliese 436b), TrES-2b, WASP-76b, or HD 189733b.
Must remain strictly non-fictional in scientific principle while employing second-person immersive framing.
Must not repeat shark longevity, octopus hearts, or relativistic time dilation.

experiment: A/B test cold-opening with an immediate lethal sensory consequence ('Your atoms would stretch into needles') versus a conceptual question hook to determine if immediate physical threat improves 3-second hold rate above 75%.
